title: Florida's 22nd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: This is an open-seat race for Florida's 22nd Congressional District following a mid-decade redistricting plan signed by Gov. Ron DeSantis. Incumbent Democrat Lois Frankel shifted her candidacy to the 23rd District, leaving no incumbent in the newly drawn 22nd District, which stretches from Broward County west across the Everglades to Marco Island on the Gulf Coast. The district leans Republican: Donald Trump won it 55%-44% in 2024, though Joe Biden carried the same territory 51%-48% in 2020. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Lean Republican,' making it a key battleground for control of the U.S. House. The primary election is scheduled for August 18, 2026, and the general election will be held on November 3, 2026.
polling_note: No general election match-up polls were available for this race as of mid-June 2026. A May 2026 TPSI poll surveyed the Republican primary field but did not include general election match-ups.

candidates.name: Pia Dandiya
candidates.summary: Pia Dandiya is a Democratic candidate for Florida's 22nd Congressional District. She shifted her campaign to this open seat in May 2026 after initially running in the 21st District. Dandiya began her career as a public school teacher through Teach for America, later founded and became principal of a high school in Harlem, New York, served as a White House Fellow at the U.S. Department of Education, and worked as an executive at Apple leading public sector education initiatives. She had raised over $1.2 million for her campaign as of March 2026.

candidates.name: Deborah Adeimy
candidates.summary: Deborah Adeimy is a Republican candidate for Florida's 22nd Congressional District. She works as a fiduciary and investment advisor and holds a BSBA in Finance. Adeimy previously ran for this seat in 2024, when the race ended in a recount. She has signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge, supporting a constitutional amendment to limit congressional terms.

candidates.name: Casey Askar
candidates.summary: Casey Askar is a Republican candidate for Florida's 22nd Congressional District. He is a Naples-based businessman and longtime supporter of Donald Trump who built a company from scratch into a portfolio of hundreds of companies across 26 states, serving as Chairman and CEO of the Askar Family Office. Askar previously ran unsuccessfully for Congress in a Gulf Coast district in 2020 and has reported assets in the range of approximately $80 million to $400 million.

candidates.name: Michael Carbonara
candidates.summary: Michael Carbonara is a Republican candidate for Florida's 22nd Congressional District. He is the former CEO of the digital banking platform Ibanera and has loaned his campaign $2.3 million, planning a $3 million advertising effort across broadcast, cable, and streaming platforms. Carbonara has been endorsed by Weston Mayor Margaret Brown and Coconut Creek Commissioner John Brody, and originally planned to challenge Democratic Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz before switching to the open 22nd District.

candidates.name: Michael Thompson
candidates.summary: Michael Thompson is a Republican candidate for Florida's 22nd Congressional District. He is a former Lee County Republican Party chair and an ally of former National Security Adviser Michael Flynn. Thompson has positioned himself as an America First candidate focusing on veterans, farmers, families, and small business owners, and has signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge.
